profile.campus: Wappingers Falls, Dutchess County, New York (CyrusOne NYM7)
profile.address: 155 Myers Corners Rd, Wappingers Falls, NY 12590
profile.reading:
Per CyrusOne's own campus page, NYM7 sits at 155 Myers Corners Rd, Wappingers Falls, NY 12590, publishing 100,000 sq ft and 3 MW of total IT capacity.

Wikipedia's CyrusOne entry states the company acquired Cervalis, a Connecticut-area data center and colocation provider, in July 2015 for approximately $400 million; this Hudson Valley, New York facility, alongside CyrusOne's Norwalk, CT site, is the most likely origin of CyrusOne's presence in this Connecticut/Hudson Valley cluster, though the operator's own materials fetched this session did not individually confirm the Wappingers Falls building by name in that acquisition story. CyrusOne was founded in July 2000 by David Ferdman and Larry Bursten and was taken private in 2022 when Kohlberg Kravis Roberts (KKR) and Global Infrastructure Partners (GIP) acquired the company for approximately $15 billion.

Since going private under KKR and GIP ownership in 2022, CyrusOne has continued expanding its US and international footprint; the company's own press materials cite roughly $1 billion in cumulative capital investment in its San Antonio, Texas campuses alone as of a January 2025 groundbreaking, indicating continued growth investment across its portfolio under private ownership rather than a broad slowdown following the take-private transaction.

In November 2021, KKR and GIP first announced the agreement to acquire CyrusOne in an approximately $15 billion transaction, one of the largest data center M&A deals of that period, reflecting broader private-equity and infrastructure-fund interest in colocation real estate that has also driven acquisitions of peers like QTS (by Blackstone) and CoreSite (by American Tower) around the same era; CyrusOne's current published portfolio language describes more than 50 mission-critical facilities worldwide, though the company's own site and Wikipedia give somewhat different approximate totals (over 40 versus more than 50), neither of which this registry treats as a precise, independently verified figure.

reading.body:
The only New York State data center in this database with a published power figure offers 3 MW of IT capacity, equivalent to roughly 75 racks at AI training density, making it too small to support a modern AI cluster alone.

NYM7 is a conventional colocation facility rather than a hyperscale campus. Its 100,000 square feet of technical space and SSAE 16 Type II certification indicate it was built to serve multiple tenants with standard operational controls, not optimized for the dense, single-purpose compute deployments AI requires. No total campus power budget is published, obscuring whether the facility has headroom to grow.

New York State shows 31 additional mapped data centers that publish no power figures. The state's true computational capacity is unknown. NYM7 and its regional cluster likely trace to CyrusOne's 2015 acquisition of Cervalis, a Connecticut colocation provider, meaning this footprint reflects legacy infrastructure rather than new AI-scale build-out. The absence of power transparency across the state makes it impossible to assess whether the Northeast corridor has the electrical supply needed to compete for AI compute deployment.
